title: What Readers Need vs. What You Need
use_cases: Use when compiling a comprehensive worldbuilding bible that includes all rules and background details necessary for consistency.
Use when drafting a manuscript to include only the information readers need to understand the plot and characters.
Use when separating background data from plot-relevant content to prevent reader confusion.
Use when designing immersive world details that are invisible to readers but support the story.
Use when maintaining a consistent rule set to avoid contradictions in the narrative.
content:
You (the author) need: • Complete understanding of how everything works • Rules that remain consistent • Background that informs character decisions • Details that prevent contradictions

Readers need: • Enough to understand what's happening • Rules relevant to the plot • Cultural context that affects characters • Details that create immersion, not confusion

Your worldbuilding bible should contain everything YOU need. Your manuscript should contain only what READERS need. The bible is 90% iceberg below water—most of it supports the story invisibly.
